title: Impact of Oxygen Non-Stoichiometry on Near-Ambient Temperature Ionic Mobility in Polaronic Mixed-Ionic-Electronic Conducting Thin Films

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Effect of oxygen non-stoichiometry on near-ambient ionic mobility in polaronic MIEC thin films is unknown. Changing the quenched-in Pr3+/Pr4+ ratio (delta) should change near-ambient oxygen-vacancy mobility via defect interactions.
states.detail: Absorbed: s1 (HYP/gap), s2 (HYP/hypothesis), s3 (DES/base_system), s4 (DES/variable_sweep), s5 (DES/method), s6 (PRC/deposition), s7 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Quenched films hold delta 0.032-0.042, with Pr3+ and oxygen vacancies ([Pr3+]=2[VO]) rising with reduction. Fewer neutral Pr3+-VO-Pr3+ tripoles are quenched in after high-T reduction (0.042) than after long low-T oxidising anneals
states.detail: Absorbed: s10 (STR/defect/point), s12 (STR/defect/point). Premises: Small-polaron conductivity peaks at [Pr3+]=[Pr4+]; on the p-side it falls as the film is reduced; Beer-Lambert with Pr4+ extinction coefficient 5.01e-18 cm2 at 532 nm plus [Pr3+]=2[VO] converts transmission to delta; Dopant-vacancy association in ceria/zirconia sets in near 300-400 C and traps vacancies

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Neutral tripoles constrict oxygen-vacancy migration pathways, lowering the mobility pre-exponential factor. Mobility pre-exponential factor rises about two decades (~40 to ~5600 cm2/Vs) from delta 0.032 to 0.042.
states.detail: Absorbed: m2 (MEC/pathway), p3 (PRP/value), p2 (PRP/value), t1 (MEC/tradeoff), p1 (PRP/value). Premises: Dopant-vacancy association in ceria/zirconia sets in near 300-400 C and traps vacancies

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Raising oxygen non-stoichiometry raises near-ambient vacancy mobility in PCO films mainly through a prefactor tied to quenched-in defect ordering

nodes.title: ECHEM:EIS, F4
nodes.head: Nyquist spectra at 50-100 C show one dominant semicircle plus a small low-frequency arc. Bulk sigma_e*T ranks 0.032 > 0.035 > 0.039 > 0.042 at every T; ~1.25 decades apart at 60 C
nodes.note: the low-frequency electrode arc is only a short tail at the high-Z' end; peak frequencies 15-59 kHz in the inset table; arcs grow as T falls 100 to 50 C (moved from label) grey '>0.05' series (never mentioned in text) lies just under 0.032 with 0.38 eV, off the monotonic p-side trend; text quotes sigma_e = 1.16e-4 S/cm, which is the plotted sigma_e*T in S K/cm

nodes.head: Hysteretic I-V loops with current peaks at both polarities that change with sweep rate 4-10 mV/s
nodes.note: peaks near +/-1.2-1.7 V, 10-15 uA; sample delta 0.032 and 60 C from caption

nodes.title: evidence, F5, F6
nodes.head: Reciprocal sweep rate is linear in t_peak^2; slope gives mu_i = 1.46e-12 cm2/Vs at 60 C. mu_i*T ranks 0.042 > 0.039 > 0.035 > 0.032 at every T, ~1.3 decades between extremes.
nodes.solves: Oxygen-vacancy mobility rises with delta at 50-100 C, ~1.2-1.3 decades from 0.032 to 0.042
nodes.op: compare across conditions, fit model, read characteristic point, read trend, replot derived series
nodes.note: five points; mu_i*T = 4.9e-10 matches the F6a delta 0.032 point at 60 C 100 C: -6.93 vs -8.27; 50 C: -8.60 vs -9.84 (log units) grey series, 0.74 eV; the most reduced film would be expected highest if mobility tracked delta alone; also a fifth point in F6c negative intercepts put mu_i*T -> 0 near delta ~0.03; lowest-delta points plotted at ~0.031; caption slope 2.75e-7 vs text 2.15e-7; caption '50-700 C' is 50-100 C; '>0.05' sample omitted
nodes.detail: o15: Reciprocal sweep rate is linear in t_peak^2; slope gives mu_i = 1.46e-12 cm2/Vs at 60 C; o18: mu_i*T ranks 0.042 > 0.039 > 0.035 > 0.032 at every T, ~1.3 decades between extremes; o19: The '>0.05' series sits below 0.035 and above only 0.032, breaking the rise of mobility with delta; o20: At each T from 50 to 100 C, mu_i*T rises with delta and is fitted linearly, slopes 2e-7 to 1e-5
nodes.inner_audit: o19: grey series, 0.74 eV; the most reduced film would be expected highest if mobility tracked delta alone; also a fifth point in F6c
